title: Samsung is testing a feature that changes the angle of photos you’ve already taken
summary:
Android Authority found code in the beta for One UI 9.5 referring to a feature called Recompose that might let you change the angle of a photo after you've taken it. The code is part of Samsung's Photo Editor app and builds on the existing Move tool. Users would be able to toggle between Move and Recompose, the latter of which is associated with text strings reading:
Drag with one finger to change the perspective. Use two fingers to pan, zoom, and rotate.
And:
Move this slider to make background objects appear closer or farther away.

title: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
summary:
Widgets, your way. | Photo: Allison Johnson / The Verge	

Aside from dealing with my calendar, there's one thing I want AI to do: tell me if I'm about to miss the bus.
What I need is a widget. It needs to tell me real-time arrivals for the bus stop near my house. Tapping around on my phone screen to open the right app and select my stop will slow me down enough to miss a bus. I need glanceable information, and I hoped that Android's vibe-coded widget feature could help me out here. It hasn't, to my disappointment, but I still had a good time cooking up other widgets.

title: 42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats
summary:
A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling off user data as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. In a deluge of nearly identical press releases, the various AGs accuse the company of planning to auction off "the private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts - more than 2.1 million of them registered to minors - with no safeguards for the people whose conversations are being sold."

summary:
Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that's designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users. title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
summary:
In an announcement on Wednesday, the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company's "Starmind" initiative. With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space, including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency has granted for a full "constellation" of AI satellites.

title: Nothing offers a full look at its AI earbuds and charging case
summary:
Nothing is showing off a much more detailed look at its upcoming AI earbuds ahead of their December 8th release. The Ear Note buds can record your calls, while their charging case can record, transcribe, and summarize your conversations.
Like the Ear 3, the Ear Note's microphone-equipped case comes with a "Talk" button that you can use to record your own voice. There's also a new "Record" button that can record and transcribe your conversations. In a post on X, Nothing CEO Carl Pei says the button will allow you to record calls through the earbuds, and meetings through the case as a "first step toward a hardware context layer for AI."

title: Has vibe coding made open source the new normal for synths?
summary:
The emergence of powerful vibe-coding agents and tools like Reverse Engineer Anything has caused chaos in the music gear world, leaving companies scrambling to figure out how to respond. While some, like Roland, have remained silent for now, others have embraced the modding community.
